messages:
Rika: Heads-up — support alerted us to a p99 latency surge for a hosted tenant starting ~11:07 UTC. A small subset of GPU hosts in prod-pool-B are showing timeouts and occasional 502/503s. Dashboards: https://grafana.company/r/redwood/dashboard/reqs?panel=latency (internal).
Sam: Which model/route and is this on our quantized path? Any recent infra changes or model swaps?
Rika: Hosted calls to `mpt-30b-qat` on `/v1/generate`. No model rollouts in last 48h. Affected boxes: `gpu-node-b7-21` and `gpu-node-b7-22` (A100-80GB). p95 OK, p99 and tail tokens jumped. GPU memory utilization reported 90%+, p99 token gen time spiked.
Joel: I pulled `nvidia-smi` + runtime logs from 11:12 — seeing many small free chunks and intermittent `cudaMalloc` failures. Snippet: 
```
[11:11:51] runtime: cudaMalloc returned OOM while allocating 16MB
[11:11:52] allocator: free_segments: 18, largest_free: 1.9GB, total_free: 5.3GB
[11:11:53] kernel: fragmentation warnings from driver
```
Mike: Repro'd in staging by hammering long chat sessions. I used a python loop that sends incremental prompts to grow KV, and staging hit allocator fallbacks after ~120s. Repro steps: 
```bash
# fast repro (staging)
python tests/long_context_repro.py --url http://staging.api/v1/generate --threads 8 --sessions 40 --tokens-per-iter 250
# long_context_repro.py appends prompts to simulate multi-turn chat
```
Results: staging reported many small failed device allocations and increased p99.
Hannah: Do we have per-session KV telemetry? Need to confirm whether KV still scales down after generation or keeps growing due to a retention/regression.
Rika: Instrumentation shows several sessions accumulating >1.6M tokens in KV; instead of stabilizing, device allocations climb after ~1800 tokens.
Joel: I inspected recent runtime changes to KV handling and found a risky change in a legacy branch: temporary KV buffers were `reserve()`d to a large capacity and never `shrink_to_fit()` on early-exit paths. That leaves oversized chunks in the device arena and increases fragmentation over time.
Sam: Immediate actions: 1) Reroute new traffic away from the two affected hosts (evacuate). 2) Restart the runtime pods on those nodes to release device arenas. 3) Apply a temporary per-session KV cap and enable LRU eviction once cap hit.
Mike: Executed the evacuation and restarted pods. Observed p99 drop to baseline ~6 minutes after pods restarted and nodes drained. Confirmed that per-session device memory stopped trending up.
Rika: Support offered the customer a short-term dedicated lane for heavy long-context flows; customer accepted a 12h window while we patch.
Hannah: Medium-term fixes: patch runtime to call `shrink_to_fit()` on temporary KV vectors, add unit tests that simulate long-context churn, and add host-level metrics `kv_bytes_per_session` and `kv_entry_count` so we can alert earlier.
Joel: Also proposing allocator tuning: we can try switching the runtime to use `cudaMallocAsync` and an async memory pool to reduce fragmentation, plus experiment with jemalloc tunables (reduce lg_chunk, enable background maintenance threads). But those require staging validation.
Sam: For a conservative immediate change, we can set an env var patch only for pool-B runtime pods: `MALLOC_CONF=lg_chunk:22,background_thread:true,decay_time:1000` and monitor in staging before rolling to prod. Note: changing lg_chunk affects other subsystems so we must scope to runtime pods only.
Mike: Additional short-term mitigations I applied: enable a runtime config `kv_trim_threshold=8MB` (evict oldest KV frames over threshold) and a rate limit on per-session token accumulation for hosted tenants. That prevented further growth during weekend load tests.
Rika: Support logs also show a few requests that triggered embedding caching in an old codepath, creating oversized KV segments. Joel, can you add a targeted fix to guard that legacy path?
Joel: Yep — will submit a PR today that ensures that embedding caches are truncated and that temporary buffers call `shrink_to_fit()`. I’ll also add integration tests that simulate abort/early-return flows to ensure buffers don't leak.
Hannah: Operational runbook updates: I will add an "GPU fragmentation and KV growth" playbook to eng-runtime ops with steps: detect (kv_bytes growth + fragmented free blocks), immediate evacuate, restart pods, temp KV cap, and contact support. Adding an alert: if host `kv_bytes_allocated_total` rises >25% in 5m and GPU free <= 12% then page oncall.
Sam: Add observability: create a Grafana panel for `kv_entries_per_host` and `kv_bytes_allocated_total` with per-tenant breakdown (sampled) and an oncall dashboard link.
Mike: FYI I uploaded staging repro artifacts to s3://redwood-debug/frag/2429990000-repro.tar.gz (nvtop, nvidia-smi snapshots, runtime logs, pmap).
Rika: Customer confirmed latency improved after the mitigations; they saw the spike subside and timeouts drop. We'll keep monitoring and follow up once PRs are merged.
Joel: I'll open two PRs: (1) fix to shrink temp KV buffers + embedding cache guard, (2) new metrics export for kv_bytes_per_session. Hannah, can you own the runbook PR?
Hannah: Yes — creating runbook and a short post-incident checklist. Will tag the thread with postmortem label and add outreach notes for the customer.
Sam: Final note: add a unit test to the allocator integration suite to mimic repeated allocate/free patterns with small chunks — should catch regressions early.
Rika: Thanks everyone — closing the escalation for now. Please paste PR links here when ready and we’ll schedule a small canary roll for the malloc/async patch to validate on pool-B. :tada:
